opex.name: General and administrative

oneTimers: Stock-based compensation was $655M in the quarter (including $109M inside cost of revenues) — the main reason non-GAAP net income ($930M) is more than 3× the GAAP figure ($298M). The cost is real; it is paid in shares instead of cash.
Other income, net swung to $206M from a $3M expense a year ago, and interest income added $70M — together they more than doubled pre-tax profit relative to the $162M operating line.
ServiceNow AI crossed $1B in annual contract value in Q2 2026, and the company counted 123 transactions over $1M in net new ACV, up nearly 40% YoY.
otherDetail: Interest income of $70M plus other income, net of $206M — a net $276M gain outside operations.

segments.name: Subscription
segments.note: Companies paying to use the ServiceNow platform — 97% of all revenue; grew 24.5% YoY (23% in constant currency).

segments.name: Professional services
segments.note: Consultants who help customers set the platform up.

takeaways.text: Total revenue grew 24% to $3.99B and subscription revenue 24.5% — ServiceNow beat the high end of its guidance on every headline metric and raised its full-year subscription outlook.
takeaways.title: Growth accelerated

takeaways.text: Remaining performance obligations — revenue customers have signed for but not yet been billed as sales — grew 21% to $29.0B, with $13.20B due in the next 12 months.
takeaways.title: Future revenue is booked

takeaways.text: GAAP EPS was $0.29 against $0.90 non-GAAP: $655M of stock-based compensation is the biggest single difference between the two profit pictures.
takeaways.title: Two very different profits

verdict: ServiceNow grew revenue 24% to $4.0B and pushed future booked revenue to $29.0B, though $655M of stock pay kept GAAP profit to $298M.
